events.title: Nectar Feeders vs. Insect Hunters: A Closer Look at Bats
events.display_title: Nectar Feeders vs. Insect Hunters: A Closer Look at Bats
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Celebrate Pollinator Week with scientists from the Gantz Family Collections Center! Bats are often celebrated as important nighttime pollinators, but not all bats play that role. At this special session, you’ll learn about the fascinating diversity of bat diets and adaptations around the globe. Even though Chicagoland’s bats do not pollinate our local flowers, they do rely on insect pollinators as part of their diets. Stop by the Grainger Science Hub to learn more and to see a live dissection of our local bat species, and special specimens of pollinating bats from around the world, too. Guests will learn the diversity of bats and be able to recall how our local bats are not pollinators, but they are still an important part of our local ecosystem. Presenters include Lauren Johnson, Assistant Collections Manager, Mammals. Please note: this session will feature a live dissection.

events.display_title: What Insects Call Our Garden Home (and Maybe Yours Too!)
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Feel empowered to be a scientist! Check out equipment scientists use in the field to observe and document insects and see photos and specimens from the insect collections. Discover how even the smaller things in nature are important to biodiversity and learn ways you can document your own observations of nature. Aster Hasle, Lead Conservation Ecologist, and Karen Klinger, Lead GIS Analyst, Keller Science Action Center.

events.title: A Day in the Life of a Pathologist: The Science That Shapes Health
events.display_title: A Day in the Life of a Pathologist: The Science That Shapes Health
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Visit the Grainger Science Hub and meet scientists from the College of American Pathologists to  explore the role of a pathologist and examine its impact on overall health. This interactive drop-in experience will introduce the world of pathology through hands-on observation, pattern recognition, and diagnostic thinking. Visitors will rotate through stations that mirror the work pathologists do every day: examining tissues, identifying disease patterns, comparing healthy and abnormal samples, and using clues to determine diagnoses. Discover how pathology is the “detective work” of medicine, combining science, visual analytics, and classification to understand disease.

events.title: Dust from the Cosmos
events.location_address: 1400 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
events.description: Visit the Grainger Science Hub to see micrometeorites found on the roof of the Field Museum! Explore how cosmic dust can be found everywhere - from the rooftops of buildings to the deserts of Antarctica. Touch meteorites that are 4.5 billion years old and observe how a Scanning Electron Microscope can be used to identify micrometeorites. This session will be presented by Basil Saleem, Resident Graduate Student, Field Museum. --
